symptom: On ako/TestApp (11.14.0) `describe page WorkflowCommons.TaskInbox` → exec, with NO edit, passed check and reported "Replaced page": both data grids were rebuilt from mxcli's template, the Assignee(s) column's Administration.Account.FullName (through System.WorkflowUserTask_Assignees) became System.User.FullName (CE1613), the row click Forms$OpenUserTaskClientAction became a Forms$NoAction, a caption lost its second translation and the data source XPath was re-indented. Any edit to a pluggable widget did the same to every property the statement did not mention; rebuilding every pluggable widget of TestApp changed 23 distinct untouched properties. Layout rewrites rebuilt their pluggable widgets every time
cause: The #721 L4 passthrough was all-or-nothing: a widget it declined — because the statement changed it, or because the rebuilt widget named a model element the stored one did not (describe prints the specialized attribute as `WorkflowUserTask_Assignees/FullName`, which resolves against System.User) — was rebuilt whole from the template. execCreateLayout never loaded the passthrough, and describedWidgets parsed only page and snippet statements
file: mdl/executor/cmd_pages_pluggable_patch.go (pageBuilder.patchStoredPluggable, called from buildPluggable when passStoredThrough declines); cmd_pages_builder_v3.go (shadowBuild stubs child widgets); cmd_pages_pluggable_passthrough.go (describedWidgets reads CreateLayoutStmt); cmd_pages_layout_v3.go (layout rewrites load the passthrough)
fix: Patch instead of rebuild: build the widget a second time from describe's own text for the stored widget, compare both builds by property key (IDs and type pointers left out), keep the stored value of every property they agree on and write the statement's value of every one they do not, onto the stored Type (template type IDs remapped by key path; object lists merged item by item when the counts line up). A property bound to the widget's own data source (DataSourceProperty `datasource` / `../datasource`) is kept while that data source is; any other property that names model elements is kept only when the describe build names what is stored, else the patch is abandoned and the widget rebuilt as before. Widgets properties always take the statement's build (their children carry the IDs that build registered)
insight: Decide 'what did the statement change' by building twice, not by mapping MDL keywords to property keys: the engine's own mappings, defaults and editorConfig visibility rules then apply identically to both sides, so the comparison needs no table that could drift. The guard that stops a stale binding is per property and keyed on the Type's DataSourceProperty link: refs-comparing everything would have refused exactly the specialization case the issue is about, and refs-comparing nothing kept Thing.Colour after a data view moved to Other (the guard's control test fails without it). Wrong seeds to skip: a second translation is restored by canon.CarryTranslations already, so a translation-seeded test passes on main; seed state no carry knows (an unspellable action, a stored specialization, Studio Pro's PrimitiveValue "" on an expression property). Measure the blast radius with the passthrough forced off on TestApp: that sweep is what found the unchanged-widget case. Still lost, separately: a classic link button inside a column's content with an action MDL cannot spell (OpenUserTaskClientAction) — describe prints no action, and classic widgets are rebuilt
